fig01.title: Fig. 1 — The Skillware Ecosystem Architecture
fig01.caption: Figure 1. The Skillware ecosystem architecture. Self-contained Skillware registry bundles decompose know-how into five first-class primitives: Contract ( manifest.yaml ), Effect ( skill.py ), Directive ( instructions.md ), Assurance ( test_skill.py ), and Corpus (domain data and schemas). Rather than a heavyweight runtime, Skillware provides a lightweight Python loader and context framework ( SkillLoader & SkillContext ) that decouples model intelligence from agentic capability—performing automatic model adaptation across host dialects (Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama/Ollama, OpenAI, and extensible downstream adapters like AWS Bedrock and DeepSeek), gradual progressive disclosure (injecting full playbooks only upon tool selection), and scoped execution context ( ctx ) without global environment mutation.

fig02.title: Fig. 2 — Anatomy of a Skill Bundle
fig02.caption: Figure 2. Anatomy of a Skillware skill bundle, exemplified by finance/uk_companies_house_handler . Know-how is decomposed into five first-class primitives rather than monolithic prompts: Contract ( manifest.yaml declares 12 typed actions, parameter JSON schemas, and permissions), Effect ( skill.py implements deterministic API execution, pagination, and bounded in-memory bytes), Directive ( instructions.md provides SOP guidance, disambiguation rules, and progressive disclosure), Assurance ( test_skill.py provides hermetic pytest fixtures and schema consistency invariants), and Corpus ( data/ stores domain reference lexicons such as UK/US terminology mappings). This atomic structure enables portable loading across diverse host agent runtimes with zero external dependencies.

fig03.title: Fig. 3 — Chained Skill Execution Across Difficulty Tiers
fig03.caption: Figure 3. Chained skill execution in the Tier 4 multi-skill crucible ( chained_pipeline_crucible.py ). A customer memo traverses a sequential multi-skill DAG: compliance/pii_masker strips confidential identifiers; a deterministic contract gate validates the intermediate envelope ( status == "ready" ); on success, clean parameters pass to finance/uk_companies_house_handler to resolve corporate registration numbers and statutory directors; monitoring/token_limiter enforces the operational token budget. Failures drop into a deterministic needs_input disambiguation loop rather than leaking raw errors or unmasked PII into downstream contexts. Cryptographic AURA Merkle receipts seal the multi-skill audit trail before final output emission.

fig05.caption: Figure 5. The empirical parameter paradox. Across three decades of parameter scale (8B to 550B+), Skillware-equipped models maintain a decisive performance wedge over unequipped baselines. The wedge is widest for compact sovereign models: an equipped Qwen 3.8 Flash (16B) or Gemma 4 (31B) achieves a perfect 16/16 (100.0%) pass rate, outscoring unequipped frontier models Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Luna (both 14/16, 87.5%) at roughly 1/30th the operational cost. Without skillware, unequipped frontier models plateau below 90% due to boundary failures on unconstrained tool contracts, whereas compact workhorses equipped with validated bundles eliminate execution regressions.

Red hatching denotes resident context excised from the model's inference hot path: redundant system preambles, exhaustive tool schemas, few-shot demonstration banks, and accumulated debugging history. By offloading executable skill logic (skill.py) and schema verification to deterministic host-side JIT handlers, resident prompt context collapses by 84.0% on average (from 15,400 to 2,460 tokens), slashing per-turn prefill latency and eliminating distraction-induced contract hallucination.

fig07.title: Fig. 7 — Deterministic Execution & Contract Gating
fig07.caption: Figure 7. Deterministic execution pipeline in Skillware. When an agent invokes a skill, capability is decoupled from intelligence: rather than relying on stochastic LLM code generation or open-ended prompt heuristics, execution passes through a strict Contract gate (manifest.yaml), runs pre-compiled, offline-tested Python logic inside the Effect handler (skill.py), and returns a structured response envelope (ready, needs_input, error). By delegating domain logic to deterministic Python rather than generative inference, Skillware achieves 100% reproducible verdicts, eliminates behavioral drift across model architectures, and executes complex tasks with zero logic token expenditure.
